segments.subgoal: Describe the role of requirement gathering in the interactive system development life cycle as the stage where end-user usability requirements are identified.

Explain usability requirements as non-functional interface-quality requirements relevant to interactive systems used by non-experts.
Explain why requirement gathering must begin with specified users and a specified context of use, using the ISO usability definition.
Describe the contextual inquiry method for gathering usability requirements by observing and interviewing users in their natural work context.
Explain why contextual inquiry is important for system development by showing how observed user activities determine essential features.
Summarize the main points of the lecture.
